subject: Post-demo privacy Q&A: prompt and response logging & residency
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
To: Samira Noor <snoor@healthtech.co>
Cc: Amit Reddy <amit.reddy@healthtech.co>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo privacy Q&A: prompt and response logging & residency

Hi Samira / Amit —

Thanks again for your time on today’s demo. A quick recap of the items you asked us to confirm so your security and legal teams can sign off:

1) What parts of prompts and model outputs are stored by Redwood by default?
2) Where is any stored content physically located (regions/residency)?
3) How long do we retain logged prompts/outputs and admin logs?
4) Can prompt/response logging be configured to be ephemeral or disabled for specific routes?

I don’t want to give incomplete answers over email — I’m looping in Laura (Redwood legal/compliance) and Karthik (solutions engineering) to provide precise wording and where applicable, links to our SOC2 summary and data handling FAQ.

Next steps I propose:
- Laura / Karthik to provide a short, one-paragraph confirmation we can include in your procurement packet.
- If that looks good, Samira / Legal Ops can confirm and we’ll update the HubSpot deal and draft the MSA redline.

Attachments: I’ve attached our redwood-data-handling-faq.pdf and soc2-summary.pdf for context.

Best,
Ben

Subject: Re: Post-demo privacy Q&A: prompt and response logging & residency

Thanks Ben — appreciate the recap. A few clarifying points from Legal Ops we need spelled out clearly:

A) When you say "stored by default", we need to know if any user prompt or model response is written to disk or object storage outside of ephemeral GPU memory for any hosted configuration. If yes, which of the following are written: raw prompt, tokenized prompt, model response, response confidence/metadata, request headers?

B) Residency: we need an explicit statement of which cloud regions/storage locations will hold any non-ephemeral data for hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments.

C) Retention: what is the default retention period for stored prompt/output logs, and what controls do we have to shorten/disable it? Please include whether logs for admin/audit (e.g., request traces) are retained separately and for how long.

D) For compliance, does Redwood provide an option that guarantees zero retention of customer prompts and model outputs for the hosted product (i.e., no persistent storage except ephemeral caches)?

If you can get Laura/Karthik to reply with single-line confirmations for each of A-D, that’ll simplify our procurement.

Samira
Senior Product Manager, HealthTech Co.

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Samira Noor <snoor@healthtech.co>, Legal Ops <legalops@healthtech.co>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo privacy Q&A: prompt and response logging & residency

Ben / Karthik —

Below are concise confirmations you can share with the customer. They are intentionally succinct so Legal Ops can paste into their procurement docs; happy to expand if they want more legalese.

A) Storage: For Redwood Hosted (standard offering), prompts and outputs may be written to persistent object storage only when customers opt in to features that require retention (e.g., evaluation datasets, long-term logs). By default, ephemeral inference does not persist raw prompt or response content to customer-facing object storage; inference occurs in GPU memory and transient caches. Metadata (request ID, timestamp, model variant, token count) is retained by default for observability and billing.

B) Residency: For Hosted customers, persistent storage (if enabled) is located in the cloud region you select during onboarding (us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1). Dedicated and Private deployments provide customer-managed residency — data remains in your VPC or on-prem cluster per deployment config.

C) Retention: Default retention for observability/billing metadata is 90 days. Prompt/response retention is 0 days unless explicitly enabled; when enabled, retention is configurable (30/90/365 days or custom) and can be shortened on request. Separate admin/audit traces are retained 365 days by default and are available under the enterprise compliance add-on.

D) Zero-retention option: Yes — for Hosted customers that require it, we offer an operational profile that disables persistent prompt/response logging (no writes to persistent object storage) and limits retention to ephemeral caches only. This can be documented as "no persistent storage of prompts or outputs" for procurement purposes, with the caveat that certain platform features (long-term evals, user-initiated archival) will be unavailable.

Attachments: redwood-data-handling-faq.pdf (summary), soc2-summary.pdf.

Karthik — please add any implementation notes regarding how to configure the route-level logging toggles in the Console UI/API (single-line).

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal & Compliance, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.example.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Samira Noor <snoor@healthtech.co>, Legal Ops <legalops@healthtech.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo privacy Q&A: prompt and response logging & residency

Hi Samira — quick operational notes to accompany Laura’s answers: 

- Route-level logging: In the Redwood Console you can set logging=off/ephemeral/persistent per route. The API equivalent is the route config flag "logging.mode" with values ["ephemeral","persistent","off"].
- Zero-retention profile: We create a customer profile during onboarding that sets logging.mode=ephemeral and disables archival. For hosted customers, this prevents any writes to long-term object storage.
- Audit logs: Admin/audit trails are separate and maintained under the enterprise compliance add-on; they contain request IDs and actor metadata but not full prompt text when zero-retention is enabled.

Next steps: If Samira / Legal Ops confirm they want the zero-retention profile for the initial pilot, I’ll open a ticket with onboarding to have the profile applied to your account prior to the POC. Otherwise, we can leave defaults and provide a retention SLA.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
